answer: A $40 copper bond and a vine-chained puzzle price each fake identity at $96 times its place in the vine. One funding source grows one vine, and the k-th identity on it solves a puzzle k times harder than the first, sending a ripple up it. Three rotating auditors check each VDF proof against public parameters each epoch, and one fake proof voids the whole vine and slashes every copper bond on it. 100 clones on one vine pay $96 times 1 through 100, $484,800, while 100 honest agents on their own vines pay 100 times $96, $9,600. A grapevine that bears heavier fruit the further you climb.
